guide.title: Guide
guide.intro: Choose the path closest to what you need, then dig into format, songbooks, and backups.
guide.gettingStartedBody: Armonia works with .cmd.md, .md, or .txt text files. Start from the Library if you are looking for a song, from the Player if you already have a file, or from the Editor if you want to write.
guide.pathLibrary: Search the catalog and personal songs saved on this device.
guide.pathPlayer: Open a local file and read it right away without editing it.
guide.pathSetlist: Put songs in order and prepare settings for the session.
guide.pathEditor: Create a CMD song or adjust an existing file with the preview alongside it.
guide.supportedFormatsBody: These are the files you can open, import, or generate with Armonia.
guide.supportedFormatsPortable: Data formats are portable and locally editable: songs are CMD Markdown files, while backups, libraries, songbooks, and setlists are ZIP archives with JSON metadata and songs in library/*.cmd.md.
guide.supportedFormatsBackupDirection: Armonia ZIP archive: export and import from Preferences
guide.supportedFormatsLibraryDirection: Armonia ZIP archive: export and import from the Library
guide.supportedFormatsSongbookDirection: Armonia ZIP archive: export from detail and import from the Songbooks list
guide.supportedFormatsSetlistDirection: Armonia ZIP archive: export and import from the Setlist page
guide.supportedFormatsPdfDirection: Export or print only from Editor and Player
guide.archiveFormatsBody: .arb, .arl, .asb, and .asl files use different extensions to describe their purpose, but internally they are Armonia ZIP archives. You can inspect them with a ZIP tool: personal songs are CMD Markdown files, while JSON files store structure, order, and references.
guide.archiveFormatsFullBackupContents: manifest.json, library/ with every personal song, songbooks/ with personal songbooks, setlists/, and preferences/favorites.json.
guide.archiveFormatsLibraryContents: manifest.json and library/ with exported personal songs. It does not contain songbooks.
guide.archiveFormatsSongbookContents: manifest.json, one songbooks/<name>/songbook.json folder, and library/ with the personal songs used by that songbook.
guide.archiveFormatsSetlistContents: manifest.json, setlist/setlist.json, and library/ with the CMD files actually used in the setlist.
guide.archiveFormatsRuleZip: Data archives are ZIP files with an Armonia extension: .arb, .arl, .asb, or .asl.
guide.archiveFormatsRuleManifest: Every archive contains manifest.json with format armonia-archive, version, scope, and export date; scope distinguishes full, library, songbook, and setlist archives.
guide.archiveFormatsRulePaths: Internal paths are relative and must not contain .. or backslashes.
guide.archiveFormatsRuleSlug: Every song in library/ must declare an explicit slug in CMD frontmatter; the exported file is named library/<slug>.cmd.md.
guide.archiveFormatsRuleReferences: JSON files reference songs using the same slug declared in the CMD, not the visible song title.
guide.archiveFormatsRuleSetlist: Setlists reference songs through songSlug; no separate source catalog metadata is saved.
guide.archiveFormatsRuleNoExtras: Archives must not contain extra files outside the expected structures, and JSON files are UTF-8 encoded.
guide.archiveFormatsExampleBody: In this example, the file name, the CMD slug, and the JSON reference all point to the same stable identifier.
guide.archiveFormatsDetailLink: Open the detailed backup formats guide.
guide.editorBody: The Editor lets you write a CMD file alongside its formatted preview.
guide.editorWrite: Write a song or open a local file; its content stays on your device.
guide.editorPreview: The preview updates as you type and displays the title, subtitle, key, links, sections, and chords.
guide.editorHints: Metadata suggestions and line diagnostics help correct common mistakes.
guide.editorLibrary: Use Save to library to keep the song as personal content on this device and find it again in the Library.
guide.editorExport: Save the .cmd.md file, open it in the Player, or generate/print a PDF from the preview.
guide.playerBody: The Player is designed for reading and performing an existing song without changing its original file.
guide.playerTranspose: Transpose the song up to 12 semitones in either direction and reset transposition using the central value.
guide.playerScroll: Start automatic scrolling and set song duration between 30 and 300 seconds.
guide.playerDisplay: Use the quick controls for transposition, autoscroll, and text size; view, chord, and notation options live in the additional controls menu.
guide.playerBasicDisplay: Use the quick controls for transposition, autoscroll, and text size.
guide.playerViews: Choose the most useful view: Lyrics + chords, Lyrics only, Chords only, or Structure.
guide.playerStructure: Structure summarizes each harmonic section and compacts repeated chord loops, for example Ab Eb Db (x2).
guide.playerEdit: Open the song in the Editor to change it, or export/print it as PDF.
guide.playerPdf: Use the PDF button to export the formatted song preview, including its title, subtitle, key, sections, lyrics, and chords.
guide.playerAndroidBack: On Android, the Back button returns to the page that opened the Player, such as the songbook you were viewing; it exits the app only when no earlier page is available.
guide.libraryBody: The Library combines the catalog included with the app and personal songs saved locally on this device.
guide.librarySearch: Search by title, author, subtitle, or lyrics; search continues to work offline.
guide.librarySource: The Catalog badge identifies songs included with the app; the Personal badge identifies your editable copies.
guide.libraryOpen: Open any song in the Player; for a personal song you can also choose Edit.
guide.libraryCopy: For a Catalog song, use Copy and edit to create a personal version without changing the original.
guide.libraryDelete: Delete is available only for personal songs and permanently removes them from the device after confirmation.
guide.libraryExport: Export library creates a portable .arl file: an Armonia ZIP archive with a manifest and all personal songs in library/*.cmd.md.
guide.libraryImport: Import library accepts a .arl file and merges songs into the personal library: songs with the same slug are overwritten with the archive version.
guide.songbooksBody: Songbooks are local collections arranged into sections, useful for repertoires, services, or set lists.
guide.songbooksCreate: Create a personal songbook and give it a unique name.
guide.songbooksSections: Add sections with a name, position and, when helpful, an identifying letter.
guide.songbooksSongs: Add songs from the Library and choose their number in the section manually.
guide.songbooksSearch: Internal search finds songbook songs by title, author, subtitle, or lyrics.
guide.songbooksExport: From a personal songbook detail page, Export songbook creates a portable .asb file: an Armonia ZIP archive with a manifest, the songbook structure, and personal songs as .cmd.md files.
guide.songbooksImport: From the Songbooks list, Import songbook restores one exported personal collection file; before it is created, you can confirm its name or choose a new one. It does not accept a complete backup.
guide.songbooksImportExisting: If an imported song has the same slug as a personal song already saved, the local version is kept and linked.
guide.songbooksCatalog: Catalog songbooks can be viewed but not changed; personal songbooks can be fully managed.
guide.setlistGuideBody: Setlists keep song sequences for rehearsals, services, or performances, with independent settings for each item.
guide.setlistGuideCreate: Create and save multiple named setlists; you can reopen, rename, or duplicate them from the list.
guide.setlistGuideAdd: Add songs from the Library by searching the catalog and your personal songs. You can add the same song more than once.
guide.setlistGuideReorder: Use Up and Down to change song order without modifying the Library or songbooks.
guide.setlistGuideSettings: For each song you can set transposition, text size, and autoscroll duration; duplicates keep separate settings.
guide.setlistGuidePlayer: Open a setlist song in the Player and use previous/next to move through the sequence.
guide.setlistGuideExport: Export creates a self-contained .asl file: an Armonia ZIP archive with a manifest, the setlist structure, and songs as .cmd.md files.
guide.setlistGuideImport: Import adds a new saved setlist without replacing the ones already stored.
guide.setlistGuideVolatile: Every change is saved automatically in the local database; use .asl to transfer one setlist and a full backup to preserve all of them.
guide.preferencesBody: Preferences define the defaults used by the Player and preview, and let you manage your personal library backup.
guide.preferencesLanguage: You can choose the interface language.
guide.preferencesAppearance: Theme, accent color, and chord color customize your reading view.
guide.preferencesMusic: Choose Italian or international notation, Player view, full/simplified/bass chords, the split-word filler, autoscroll speed, and text size.
guide.preferencesBasicMusic: You can adjust autoscroll speed and text size.
guide.preferencesLocal: Preferences are stored locally in this device's browser.
guide.preferencesBackupExport: Export backup creates an .arb file: an Armonia ZIP archive with a manifest, personal songs, songbooks, and saved setlists.
guide.preferencesBackupImport: Import backup accepts only a complete backup and restores it atomically, without leaving a partial import if an error occurs.
guide.preferencesBackupConflict: When importing a complete backup, a local song with the same slug takes precedence over the one in the file; a songbook whose name is already present is imported with the import date and time appended to its name. When importing one songbook, you can choose its name.
guide.preferencesDevelopmentDataWarning: This version is still stabilizing: after database structure changes, you may need to manually clear local data and import it again from a backup.
guide.cmdBody: CMD (Chord Markdown) is a text format: optional frontmatter contains metadata, ## headings divide sections, and chords in square brackets are positioned within lyric lines.
guide.metadataIntro: Put metadata between two --- lines at the start of the file.
guide.metadataSlug: Text identifier for the song. If omitted on save, it is generated from author and title.
guide.metadataKey: Key in the selected notation, for example C or DO.
guide.metadataTags: Comma-separated labels. Liturgical categories accept canonical keys and Italian aliases such as liturgia:tempo:pasqua.
guide.metadataLinks: External links, preferably one per indented line.
guide.sectionsBody: Any Markdown heading from # through ###### creates a section; names are free-form, such as Intro, Verse, Chorus, or Bridge.
guide.chordsBody: Write chords in square brackets where they begin over the lyrics. Italian and international notation, minor chords marked with m or -, accidentals, extensions, and slash bass notes are supported. Use dim or ° for diminished chords, dim7 or °7 for diminished sevenths, and ø, ø7, m7b5, min7b5 or -7b5 for half-diminished chords. Simple mode keeps dim and m7b5 (or -7b5).
guide.spacingBody: One or more blank lines inside a section produce a single visual break in the song. Blank lines near the beginning or end of a section are ignored.
guide.linksBody: The multiline form keeps files easier to read. YouTube, Spotify, audio, and website have dedicated icons in the preview.
guide.linksNote: Other types with an http or https URL are accepted and displayed as web links. The pdf type is reserved for app export and is ignored in metadata.

guide.examplePreviewBody: This is the result of processing the CMD file shown above.
guide.examplePreviewPdf: Use the PDF button in the preview corner to export the formatted song.

archiveFormatsDetail.title: Detailed backup formats guide
archiveFormatsDetail.intro: This page describes the internal structure of Armonia archives. Use it when you want to inspect a backup, generate an archive manually, or understand how songs, songbooks, and setlists are linked.
archiveFormatsDetail.commonRulesIntro: All data formats follow a small shared rule set, so archives remain readable and verifiable outside the app too.
archiveFormatsDetail.ruleZip: .arb, .arl, .asb, and .asl files are ZIP archives with an Armonia extension.
archiveFormatsDetail.ruleManifest: Every archive contains manifest.json with format armonia-archive. The scope field distinguishes full, library, songbook, and setlist.
archiveFormatsDetail.rulePaths: Internal paths are relative: .., absolute paths, and backslashes are not allowed.
archiveFormatsDetail.ruleSlug: Personal songs live in library/<slug>.cmd.md and the same slug must be declared in the CMD frontmatter.
archiveFormatsDetail.ruleReferences: JSON song references use the stable slug, not the title or display name.
archiveFormatsDetail.ruleOfficial: In songbooks, source: "official" references a catalog song included in the app; source: "user" references a personal song present or linked by slug.
archiveFormatsDetail.ruleSetlist: .asl setlists do not save source: every item uses songSlug and the archive contains the required CMD files in library/.
archiveFormatsDetail.ruleJson: JSON files are UTF-8 encoded and archives must not contain extra files outside the expected structures.
archiveFormatsDetail.arbPurpose: An .arb stores the whole personal library, personal songbooks, setlists, and favorite songs present on the device at export time.
archiveFormatsDetail.arbImport: It is imported from Preferences. The operation accepts only complete backups and is applied atomically, avoiding partial imports when the archive is invalid.
archiveFormatsDetail.arbNoteLibrary: library/ contains personal songs exported as CMD Markdown.
archiveFormatsDetail.arbNoteSongbooks: songbooks/ contains zero or more personal songbooks; official songs remain references to the app catalog.
archiveFormatsDetail.arbNoteSetlists: setlists/ contains zero or more setlists with order and settings; importing does not choose an active setlist.
archiveFormatsDetail.arbNoteFavorites: preferences/favorites.json stores source + slug references for songs marked with a star.
archiveFormatsDetail.arlPurpose: An .arl exports personal songs only, without songbooks or setlists.
archiveFormatsDetail.arlImport: It is imported from the Library. Personal songs already present with the same slug are overwritten by the archive version.
archiveFormatsDetail.arlNoteOverwrite: The slug is the identity key: when it matches, local content is updated.
archiveFormatsDetail.asbPurpose: An .asb makes one personal songbook portable together with the personal songs it needs.
archiveFormatsDetail.asbImport: It is imported from the Songbooks list. Before the songbook is created, you can confirm its name or choose a new one.
archiveFormatsDetail.asbNoteSingleSongbook: There must be exactly one songbooks/<normalized-name>/songbook.json file.
archiveFormatsDetail.asbNoteLibrary: library/ contains only the personal songs referenced by the exported songbook.
archiveFormatsDetail.aslPurpose: An .asl stores a setlist with order, per-item settings, and the CMD files needed to read it on another device.
archiveFormatsDetail.aslImport: It is imported from the Setlist list and creates a new saved setlist.
archiveFormatsDetail.aslNoteManifest: The manifest uses format armonia-archive and scope setlist.
archiveFormatsDetail.aslNoteSongSlug: Each item must declare complete id, title, songSlug, and settings fields; songSlug must match the slug in the CMD present in library/.
archiveFormatsDetail.aslNoteDuplicates: Two items may use the same songSlug: they remain distinct items and keep separate settings.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Armonia is designed to operate locally in the browser and in the Android app. This notice describes processing connected with use of the app.
privacy.controllerBody: The controller for processing determined by the app is the publisher of Armonia. Before public distribution of the app, this section will provide a private contact channel for privacy requests and the exercise of rights.
privacy.localFilesBody: When you open a .cmd.md, .md, or .txt file, its content is read locally by the app only to generate the preview, player, and print view. The app does not upload the file to a server.
privacy.noBackendBody: Armonia does not use an application backend to store songs, songbooks, accounts, or history, and does not integrate its own analytics, advertising, or profiling systems. Library content remains on your device unless you export or share it.
privacy.storageBody: The app locally stores language, theme, and player preferences. Personal songs, metadata, links, songbooks, and setlists are saved in an SQLite database on the device; in the browser persistence uses local storage/IndexedDB.
privacy.purposesBody: Local data is processed only to provide the requested functions: editing and reading songs, offline search, organizing songbooks, preferences, export, and restoration. Where the GDPR applies, processing is necessary to provide the service requested by the user under Article 6(1)(b) GDPR. No consent is requested for marketing or tracking purposes, which the app does not perform.
privacy.exportBody: When you save a .cmd.md file, generate a PDF, or export .arb, .arl, .asb, or .asl files, the content is produced locally on the device. You decide where to store or share it.
privacy.retentionBody: Preferences, songs, songbooks, and setlists remain on the device until you delete them in the app, clear app or site data on the device/browser, or uninstall the app. Exported files and shared copies remain in the locations you choose and must be deleted from those locations separately.
privacy.securityBody: Library data is separated from the distributed catalog. Importing a library explicitly overwrites personal songs with the same slug; backups and songbooks use conservative rules. The app database is not encrypted at application level: protecting the device, browser, exported backups, and any services through which you share them remains important.
privacy.hostingBody: If you use the Web version hosted on GitHub Pages, GitHub may process technical connection data, such as IP address, browser information, and access logs, as hosting provider and in accordance with its own privacy statement. If you obtain the app through a store or another platform, that platform may process data related to downloads, updates, or accounts under its own terms.
privacy.transfersBody: Armonia does not transfer personal library content to its own servers. For the Web version, any technical processing performed by GitHub may involve international transfers governed by GitHub in its privacy statement.
privacy.thirdPartyBody: Bootstrap and icons are included in the app assets. Music or web links in song metadata are opened only when you select them; once opened, the destination site processes connection data under its own privacy notice.
privacy.rightsBody: For data stored only on your device, you can directly access, export, correct, or delete songs, songbooks, and backups using app and device functions. For processing attributable to the controller, you may request, where applicable, access, rectification, deletion, restriction, portability, and objection using the privacy contact that will be published before distribution.
privacy.complaintBody: If you believe that personal data processing infringes the GDPR, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority. In Italy, you can contact the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali.
